blogs.title: When B12 Isn’t the Whole Story: Pancytopenia, Low Retics, and the Telomere Trap
blogs.description: Severe B12 deficiency explained a lot—until it didn’t. This post walks through the pitfall of anchoring on nutritional anemia when pancytopenia, a very low reticulocyte count, and multisystem premature-aging features persist, and shows how telomere biology disorders (TBDs) can masquerade as simple ineffective erythropoiesis.

blogs.title: IPF in Your 20s? Think Telomeres: Recognizing TBD Without the Dyskeratosis Triad
blogs.description: Young-onset pulmonary fibrosis and hepatic fibrosis with cytopenias should flip the telomere switch—even when the classic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita is absent. Practical red flags, targeted history and exam, and a streamlined diagnostic approach (including when to order telomere length testing and genetics) are covered.

blogs.title: PARN-ticularly Important: What Monoallelic PARN Variants Mean at the Bedside
blogs.description: A quick tour of PARN biology and why monoallelic variants can present with pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic fibrosis, and marrow vulnerability. We’ll translate genotype-to-phenotype (biallelic vs monoallelic), incomplete penetrance, and how a PARN variant of uncertain significance can still guide surveillance and counseling.

blogs.title: DAT-Positive, Not Hemolytic: The Hemolysis Red Herring in Ineffective Erythropoiesis
blogs.description: A positive DAT and indirect hyperbilirubinemia can mislead you toward autoimmune hemolysis. Learn how to distinguish immune destruction from intramedullary hemolysis due to ineffective erythropoiesis—using retic response, marrow findings, iron indices, and clinical context—so you don’t chase steroids when you need to fix the marrow (and look for TBD).

blogs.title: Pancytopenia Algorithm 2.0: Add Telomere Biology to Your Adult Workup
blogs.description: Most adult algorithms stop at nutrition, infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy, and classic marrow failure. This post adds an inherited layer: when normal cytogenetics, low retics, premature aging features, or fibrotic organs appear, build in telomere length testing and a TBD gene panel—so you don’t miss a transplant- and family-impacting diagnosis.

blogs.title: Silent Cirrhosis in Short Telomere Syndromes: Don’t Forget the Liver
blogs.description: Hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis are under-recognized in TBDs and not limited to TERC/TERT. We cover who to screen, how to use transient elastography, avoidance of hepatotoxins (including androgen therapy caveats), vaccination and variceal/HCC surveillance considerations in patients with suspected or confirmed telomere disease.

blogs.title: ILD in the Young Adult: Genetics, Family Screening, and Transplant Nuances in TBD
blogs.description: How to approach interstitial lung disease under 40: when to suspect a telomere disorder, how to involve genetics, and why telomere length informs antifibrotic therapy, immunosuppression risk, and lung transplant candidacy. We discuss conditioning toxicity, cytopenia risk, and why ‘standard’ regimens can be dangerous in short telomere patients.

blogs.title: Treating the Untreatable? Androgens, HSCT, and Management Landmines in Telomere Disorders
blogs.description: Danazol and nandrolone can lengthen telomeres in small studies, but at a hepatic cost—particularly relevant when fibrosis is already present. We outline who might benefit, monitoring strategies, when to consider hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and how to tailor conditioning to avoid catastrophic toxicity in TBD.

blogs.title: Making Sense of a VUS: Using Phenotype to Move the Needle in Suspected TBD
blogs.description: A monoallelic PARN variant labeled “uncertain” doesn’t mean clinically irrelevant. We show how phenotype matching, domain location, population rarity, and telomere length can up- or downshift a variant’s weight in decision-making, and how to communicate uncertainty while still acting on surveillance and family counseling.

blogs.title: The Telomere Review of Systems: Premature Aging Clues You’ll Miss If You Don’t Look
blogs.description: Premature greying, osteoporosis, neuropathy, nail/hair changes, oral lesions, and unexplained cytopenias are the breadcrumbs. Build a quick bedside ROS and exam checklist that raises pretest probability for TBDs, prompting earlier genetics and organ-specific screening before irreversible fibrosis or marrow failure sets in.
